phase3_findings.description: refresh-pr-on-resume.sh resolves DEVFLOW_GH via the execution-verified resolver but assigns it with `: "${DEVFLOW_GH:=$(devflow_resolve_gh)}"` without exporting it. The child process it shells out to for PR selection (python3 resolve-issue-pr.py) reads os.environ.get("DEVFLOW_GH") and, absent an export, falls back to bare `gh`. On a host where the resolver had to pick a non-bare candidate (e.g. gh.exe on a Windows/Git-Bash runner because bare gh is present-but-unrunnable), PR selection runs bare gh, fails, and the helper returns REFUSED resolve, silently disabling the whole note-strip + link-refresh feature while the parent's own gh calls would have succeeded. Invisible to the suite because every test passes DEVFLOW_GH already exported into the environment. Fix: export DEVFLOW_GH before the python child.

phase3_findings.description: workpad.py's hand-maintained parallel copies of the note-block transform (_strip_stopped_note_block / _add_stopped_note_block) are never executed by any test. The coupling pin asserts only that the two marker literals are byte-identical, not that the transform (separator handling, --> sanitization, strip-then-prepend replace) matches pr-note-block.py's. A silent divergence would pass the pin and ship a malformed/comment-escaping block onto a real PR body. The module is importable (the selector/swallow tests already exec_module it), so the same round-trip + sanitization assertions could be run against the twin.

## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (no Critical or self-contradicting-diff findings; five Important non-blocking items — one behavioral, four test-coverage — worth addressing)

## Issue Compliance
Reviewed against issue #2060: mirror stopped-run notes into the PR description — criteria from caller override (--issue 2060); scope not-established (standalone engine run over the local branch delta; no workpad ACS surface compared this run). The change maps cleanly to the described ACs: AC1 the gate job is wired as the single owner of the PR [View run] refresh + note strip (pinned); AC2/AC3 the block carries the recorded stop-note/reflection text (_stopped_note_text_for_mirror selects notes for Failed/Cancelled and blocked-reflection text, None for Complete and every other status — AC7); AC4 the branch-setup pre-check strips on every resume as the local-resume cleaner; AC5 add/strip round-trips byte-faithfully and is fail-closed; AC6 the workpad mirror runs after the workpad PATCH lands and swallows every exception.

## Verification Checklist Results
Phase 1/2 formal checklist fan-out was not separately dispatched in this run; the diff's claims were verified directly during Phase 3 (agents read the shipped code, not only the diff) and via the intra-diff truthfulness sweep below. engine_self_modifying is set (skills/**, agents/**, lib/** touched), so the leaner-checklist skip does not apply; treat verification as agent-and-direct rather than lite/agent-checklist tallied.

intra-diff contradiction scan: no contradiction found.
truthfulness sweep: no finding promoted.
over-grade annotation: no finding flagged.

## Code Review Findings
### 🟠 Important / Major
1. refresh-pr-on-resume.sh assigns DEVFLOW_GH via `: "${DEVFLOW_GH:=$(devflow_resolve_gh)}"` without exporting it, so the child `resolve-issue-pr.py` (which reads os.environ) falls back to bare `gh`; on a host where the resolver picked a non-bare candidate (e.g. gh.exe on a Windows/Git-Bash runner) PR selection runs bare gh, fails, and silently disables the whole feature while the parent's own gh calls succeed — invisible to the suite because tests pass DEVFLOW_GH already exported. Fix: export DEVFLOW_GH before the python child. (raised by 1/5 agents)
2. workpad.py's hand-maintained parallel note-block transform (_strip/_add_stopped_note_block) is never executed by a test — the coupling pin protects only the marker literals, not the transform logic, exactly the divergence class a single-source-forbidden copy is prone to; the module is importable so the same round-trip/sanitization assertions apply. (raised by 1/5 agents)
3. workpad.py's _resolve_open_pr_for_issue (parallel copy of the tested resolver selection) has no behavioral coverage — only stubbed out in the AC6 swallow test; a silent divergence would mirror the note onto the wrong PR with nothing red. (raised by 1/5 agents)
4. _mirror_stopped_note_to_pr happy path (resolve → read → add block → PATCH, temp-file lifecycle) is untested; only the AC6 swallow path is covered. (raised by 1/5 agents)
5. refresh-pr-on-resume.sh's REFUSED patch/read/empty-body arms are untested (only missing-args is) — these decide whether a stale banner survives on a real PR. (raised by 1/5 agents)

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor
1. The gate step warns on any non-zero exit of refresh-pr-on-resume.sh, so the benign NO_PR (exit 2) case surfaces a "did not complete" warning that reads as a fault; warn only on exit 3. (raised by 2/5 agents)
2. refresh-pr-on-resume.sh couples the note strip and link refresh in one pipeline/PATCH — a future non-zero from refresh-pr-run-link.py would discard the strip too; harmless today (that helper returns unchanged/exit-0 when no [View run] line is present). (raised by 1/5 agents)
3. devflow-implement.yml lines 21-27: over-length (7-line) workflow rationale comment under the prevention-only standard. (raised by 1/5 agents)
4. lib/test/run.sh lines 202-213: over-length (~11-line) test-file provenance comment. (raised by 1/5 agents)
5. resolve-issue-pr.py unparseable-JSON → exit 3 branch untested. (raised by 1/5 agents)
6. pr-note-block.py strip_block unterminated-start-marker branch untested. (raised by 1/5 agents)
7. workpad.py _cmd_update_inner selector→mirror junction not integration-tested. (raised by 1/5 agents)
8. `gh pr list` calls omit --limit (default cap 30) in both resolver copies — theoretical given the filter. (raised by 1/5 agents)

## Verdict Criteria
- No verification-checklist FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE.
- No self-contradicting-diff (documented_falsehood) finding — comment-analyzer and code-reviewer confirmed all diff-added docstrings/comments/changeset prose are accurate against HEAD; the intra-diff contradiction scan found none.
- No Critical findings; at the default `critical` verdict_severity_threshold, Important findings do not drive REJECT (rule 3 fires only on Critical).
- Dirty-tree backstop: clean (no working-tree divergence across the Phase 3.1 dispatch).

The one behavioral item worth acting on before merge is Important #1 (export DEVFLOW_GH), which defeats the resolver contract on non-standard runners though the feature is best-effort. The four test-coverage Importants (#2-#5) close the gap around workpad.py's deliberately hand-maintained parallel copies and the shell orchestrator's failure arms.
